result.summary: 3 exact, 7 behavioral, 0 stub parts. Logic is ok; approximate or missing: timing, analog, power, radio. Check the 20 items in testOnRealDevice on hardware before trusting it.

notes: arduino-uno: Cycle-counted at 16 MHz on a deterministic virtual clock, so delay()/millis() are exact in virtual time. Peripherals the emulator lacks (e.g. some timer modes, sleep) and the crystal's ±50 ppm drift are not modelled.

ili9341-tft: Bytes arrive at the speed of the emulated AVR SPI (8 MHz SCK max on an Uno, about 20 CPU cycles per byte with Adafruit's loop), so how long a redraw takes is realistic. The panel itself is instant: no 70 Hz refresh, no tearing, no 5 ms wait after reset or 120 ms after SLPOUT enforced (the library waits anyway).

esp01-wifi: Bit-exact UART at the module's baud rate, both directions, on the board's pins. Command delays are typical figures (join 1.5 s + 0.9 s for the IP on an open network, 3.6 s to report a wrong password, 25 ms DNS, TCP connect from the sandbox host, SSL adds its handshake time); a real module varies by hundreds of ms with the AP and the radio.
pushbutton: Switches instantly; real contacts bounce for 1–10 ms, which firmware must debounce.
buzzer: Starts and stops instantly; the internal ~2.3 kHz oscillator is not simulated cycle by cycle and there is no audio output yet.

arduino-uno: Pins are ideal sources with 25 Ω output resistance. Digital inputs use the datasheet thresholds (low ≤ 0.3·VCC, high ≥ 0.6·VCC) and keep their last level in between. The ADC reads the solved net voltage against a 5 V reference; AREF, noise and input capacitance are ignored.

ili9341-tft: Colours are RGB565 expanded to 8 bits per channel with no gamma curve, so the canvas looks more saturated than a real TN panel, which also washes out at an angle. The backlight is on/off or PWM duty.
esp01-wifi: TX drives 3.3 V through 40 Ω; RX, EN and RST have the ESP-01S 12 kΩ pull-ups. 5 V on RX is reported, not simulated as damage.
pushbutton: Closed contact is 0.01 Ω, open contact is a perfect open circuit.
buzzer: Modelled as a 180 Ω load (≈ 25 mA at 5 V) with a reverse-blocking diode; loudness ramps linearly from 3 V to 5 V.
arduino-uno: 5 V / 3.3 V rails are stiff sources. Per-pin current above 40 mA is flagged; total-package (200 mA) and regulator limits, VIN and brownout are not simulated.

ili9341-tft: Draws about 20 mA logic plus 60 mA backlight at full brightness from VCC. Losing VCC clears the controller RAM. A 3.3 V-only module reports 5 V logic as an error; electrically nothing breaks in the sim.
esp01-wifi: A constant 80 mA load on VCC. Real transmit peaks of 170 to 300 mA (which brown out an Uno's 3V3 pin and reset the module) are not modelled.
buzzer: Current draw is realistic for a 5 V active buzzer, so GPIO overcurrent checks apply.
resistor: Dissipation is computed and warned above 1/4 W; heating, derating and failure are not simulated.

esp01-wifi: No RF: the sandbox network decides joins, DNS and TCP. Signal strength is fixed at -52 dBm, there is no packet loss, retransmission or TLS certificate check, and a Wi-Fi drop is an injected fault (set esp.wifi = down) or a network-wide fault.

uno (arduino-uno): Upload through the bootloader (arduino-cli upload)
tft1 (ili9341-tft): Colours: some modules are RGB instead of BGR (red and blue swapped): try tft.invertDisplay() or a different MADCTL
tft1 (ili9341-tft): Logic level: bare red modules are 3.3 V logic; on a 5 V Uno use a level shifter (74HC4050) or the module can fail over time
tft1 (ili9341-tft): Long SPI wires above 15 cm corrupt pixels at 8 MHz; shorten them or lower the SPI clock
